narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the presence of a guarantor. The requested duration of 48 months was the most important reason for the denial. At more than twice the average length of approved loans (19 months), this long repayment period strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Your checking account status came second. Having a negative balance puts you in a relatively small group (only 13% of applicants), and this feature also increased the likelihood of being seen as high risk. 

The one factor that worked in your favor was having a guarantor. This provided some positive influence toward approval, but unfortunately it was not enough to overcome the concerns created by the long loan term and your account status.

You should consider reapplying for a substantially shorter loan, ideally closer to 18–24 months, after improving your checking account balance. This combination would likely improve your chances significantly.
